content:
Lionfish reached its Phase 1 milestone as a native Windows desktop utility under the JeffersonWM monorepo (apps/lionfish), targeting .NET 10 and WPF. Built to isolate secondary USB keypads—specifically a 34-key mechanical numpad and an 8-button macro pad with rotary knob—from the primary keyboard, Lionfish intercepts keystrokes at the kernel level so macro pads can trigger actions, media controls, and shortcuts without interfering with ordinary typing.

What was built:

  • Kernel Driver Interception & Safety Guard: Integrated the low-level Interception driver (InputInterceptorNS) for true OS-level hardware key blocking. Built-in failsafes include an emergency kill switch (simultaneous Left Ctrl + Right Ctrl), watchdog heartbeat monitoring, and automatic master keyboard protection preventing accidental lockout of the primary typing device.
  • Interactive “Press to Identify” Mode: Integrated a Windows Raw Input sink (WM_INPUT). Pressing any physical key instantly highlights that specific device card in glowing orange and displays the exact key pressed (e.g. Last key: [1]), making it easy to identify keypads before assigning roles.
  • Composite Endpoint Consolidation & Hardware Alignment: Merged composite USB interfaces sharing a physical hardware ID (e.g. standard keys and consumer control collections) into a single device card with aggregated paths. Aligned friendly hardware names to physical hardware (34-key numpad vs. 8-button macro pad with knob) and filtered out virtual software devices.
  • Custom Device Title Editing: Added an inline ✏️ edit button to device cards. Users can type custom labels (e.g. “Work Numpad”, “Stream Controller”) that persist across restarts in %APPDATA%\Lionfish\config.json.
  • Key Map Device Selector & Dark ComboBox: Connected live device scanning events directly to the Key Map dropdown selector. Keypads are automatically listed and pre-selected with starter action bindings, styled with a sleek dark-themed ComboBox and category badges.
  • Perihelion-Style Button Navigation: Restyled navigation tabs into dark pill button containers with subtle hover states and bold Lionfish orange accent pills (#FF6B35).
  • Windows 11 Smart App Control Hardening: Consolidated core interception, macro, and profile engines into a single unified binary (Lionfish.exe), bypassing Windows 11 Smart App Control blocks on secondary unsigned development DLLs.

Lionfish now reliably identifies physical keypads, prevents duplicate interface clutter, protects the master typing keyboard, and provides a polished desktop control surface ready for key mapping and browser automation.
title: Lionfish hardware keypad interceptor, device detection, and UI alignment
